title: Analysis of Nonlinear Phase Noise in Coherent Fiber-Optic Systems Based on Phase Shift Keying
abstract: Analytical expressions for the phase variance in a nonlinear fiber optic system based on phase-shift keying are developed. The Gauss-Hermite functions are used as the orthogonal basis to represent the noise field. Number of degrees of freedom (DOF) to accurately model the phase variance is estimated. The amplifier noise excites higher order Gauss-Hermite noise modes and the nonlinear mixing of a signal pulse and higher order Gauss-Hermite noise mode leads to new noise fields which enhance the nonlinear phase noise. The higher order noise modes propagate linearly and enhance the linear phase noise if the matched filter is not used at the receiver. Analytical expression for the optimum launch power is developed taking into account the linear and nonlinear phase noise.
summary: This paper develops advanced analytical techniques to quantify nonlinear phase noise in high-speed optical communication links. By expanding the noise field using Gauss-Hermite functions up to arbitrary degrees of freedom, it provides a more accurate model than previous works. The results yield an optimum launch power that minimizes overall signal degradation due to both linear and nonlinear effects.
main_problem: The paper analyzes nonlinear phase noise accumulation in coherent fiber-optic communication systems utilizing Phase Shift Keying (PSK). It aims to provide accurate analytical expressions for the phase variance by accounting for higher-order noise modes.
main_result: The inclusion of arbitrary degrees of freedom (DOFs) significantly improves the accuracy over previous two-DOF models, and an optimum launch power can be derived by balancing linear and nonlinear noise contributions.
method: The analysis uses a perturbation expansion approach on the Nonlinear Schrödinger equation, representing the noise field using Gauss-Hermite functions as an orthogonal basis set.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as an amplified optical link governed by the NLS equation, where noise arises from Amplified Spontaneous Emission (ASE) at discrete amplifier locations. The analysis extends beyond simple two-DOF approximations to arbitrary DOFs.
key_observables: Phase variance ($\langle\delta\phi^2angle$), optimum launch power ($P_{opt}$), and Bit Error Rate (BER).
important_parameters: Dispersion profile ($ eta_2(z)$), nonlinear coefficient ($\gamma$), number of amplifiers ($N_a$), and the number of degrees of freedom (DOFs).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a pseudo-linear regime where nonlinearity is treated as a first-order perturbation, and it assumes signal power is much greater than mean ASE power.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of phase variance on the number of DOFs (matched vs. Gaussian filters) and show how variance changes with total length or launch power for specific dispersion parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops analytical expressions by expanding the noise field using Gauss-Hermite functions, deriving formulas for the phase variance considering arbitrary DOFs, and finally determining the optimum launch power that minimizes this accumulated noise.
why_interesting: While focused on classical communication systems, the mathematical framework—using orthogonal function expansions (Gauss-Hermite) to model complex noise accumulation in a nonlinear wave equation—shares conceptual parallels with analyzing quantum noise or decoherence channels in open quantum systems.
